text: SHEET LINE FIXED AT THE SOURCE 2026-11-05. Root cause was ONE LINE in tools/gen_char_sheet.py: the shared template told every character 'Render it in the technicolor 80s sword-and-sandals register: practical leather-and-brass costume' while also saying 'Keep the costume of <Picture 1>' - the explicit wardrobe words won, so 13 characters whose film canon is purple robes, ochre hide, red tunics, white/blue garments all came back in brown leather with gold studs, and the invented extra people in the group-scene renders wore that same brown. Proven with a 3-take test on TEEGRA queued to the 5090 (same graph/seed, one variable apart) and judged by goldfishbowl's 32B: A control (graph untouched) reproduces brown; B (leather-and-brass clause removed + film costume named) returns PURPLE; C (B + LoRA 1.05 -> 0.6) identical to B, so the retro-fantasy style LoRA was INNOCENT. Then patched the generator to inject each character's own refs/characters/<NAME>/traits.txt first line as an authoritative CANON line (and refuse to render at all if a character has no non-empty traits.txt - that refusal is the guard against ever repeating this) and re-rendered the whole 13-character line as take t02 on the 5090, keeping t01 on disk: 13/13 rendered (~2 min each). Re-audited against canon (manifests/sheet_traits_audit_t02.jsonl): costumes now read as canon across the board - TEEGRA purple two-piece, NEKRON purple open-front robe, TUTOR ochre-brown hide tunic WITH the woven vest and bone toggles, JAROL and TARO red tunic, ROLIEL white top over blue with the beaded collar, JULIANA purple V-neck, ENVOY purple robe with black lining, SUBHUMAN black loincloth, SUBHUMAN CAPTAIN shirtless, DARKWOLF brown leather with fur trim AND now the wolf's head. Remaining flags are detail-level (material wording, TARO's pants, ornament specifics). ALSO FIXED because it would have silently undone everything: sheet_path() in runs/build_technicolor_ref2va.py returned the FIRST SORTED sheet, so after t02 every render would still have consumed the brown t01 generation - it now takes the newest take (pin/roll back with FNI_SHEET_GLOB='{name}_sheet_t01*.png'); the chosen filename lands in the render graph so each clip's provenance shows its sheet generation. Also hardened core/gf_client.py: a non-existent image PATH used to be shipped as raw base64 and came back as a server-side 400 'Failed to process image', which reads like a broken box - it now raises. That cost me a false 'goldfishbowl images are broken again' diagnosis tonight (the real cause was a misplaced underscore in a filename; the box was fine, 32B loaded at n_ctx 32768). Caveat on t02: it encodes the 9 film-derived traits.txt DRAFTS which Alex has not ruled; amending a draft = re-render that character's sheet (one command). Coord board row 13 updated and pushed 27315e7. Next: Alex rules the 9 drafts, then the 134 missing audio-led takes can be re-queued on the corrected sheets.

Alex on T0017 (2026-11-05): 't0017 is the best so far. some of the dialog prompts got messed up, nekron was speaking juliannas lines, but the video and prompting looked the best. if we had used better character sheets it would have been really close.'
Alex on the TEEGRA sheet-realism montage (2026-11-05): '2 they are like half and half drawn photo' — panel 2 (H3 realism wording, cel ref, LoRA 1.05) reads as a half-drawn/half-photo blend.

SHEET REALISM SOLVED as a two-stage chain (2026-11-05). Alex's ruling: 'we need to give realistic not illustrated character sheets to h3'. Measured ladder (TEEGRA, same seed, one variable per take, judged by the 32B): cel ref + design-sheet wording -> ILLUSTRATION; cel ref + realism wording at LoRA 1.05 / 0.5 / 0.0 -> ALL THREE still ILLUSTRATION (so neither the wording nor the retro-fantasy LoRA is what makes the sheets drawn); photoreal ref (Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 of the film frame, run on the 4090 via tools/qwen_scene.py, ckpt Qwen-Rapid-AIO-NSFW-v22) + realism wording + LoRA 1.05 -> MIXED; photoreal ref + LoRA 0.0 -> PHOTOGRAPH ('high-resolution photograph, realistic lighting, skin texture and fabric details, consistent with professional studio photography'). ROOT CAUSE: H3 ref2va reproduces its REFERENCE'S MEDIUM, and EVERY TEEGRA reference on disk is an illustration (id_TEEGRA.jpg 'bold outlines and flat colors', shot_00270 'stylized non-photorealistic artwork', even the cosplay ref). So the fix is the input, not the prompt: (1) Qwen-Edit the film frame to a photoreal person in canon costume, (2) run gen_char_sheet --realism --lora-strength 0.0 --still <that photo>. New flags added: gen_char_sheet --realism / --lora-strength / --still. Instrument caveat recorded: the 32B calls every AI image 'not a photograph', so photograph-vs-illustration is Alex's eye call; the VLM is only reliable for the specific complaints (line work, flat shading). Montages for his eye: runs/TEEGRA_sheet_realism/TEEGRA_sheet_realism_comparison.png (round 1, panels 1-5) and TEEGRA_sheet_realism_round2.png (3000x1600, labelled). Skill fni-h3-pipeline updated with the ladder + two-stage recipe. Pending his ruling on which panel to adopt, then the whole 13-sheet line regenerates through the chain.

Alex on the T0017 dialogue notation (2026-11-05), correcting me for the second time: '(S1)' is not subject 1, it is the FIRST SPEAKER in that prompt, and it is per prompt — if the first speaker is subject 3, then that speaker is S1 and stays s1 for the whole prompt (his first phrasing had the s3/s1 slip, then he corrected to 'they stay s1 for the whole prompt').

FIXED the (S#) speaker-id bug across every prompt builder (2026-11-05). Rule (official: docs/h3-official ref guide 5.4 'the ID comes from the target video's global speaker order and is not independently assigned or renumbered', example '<Subject 2> (S1) turns toward the woman and says'; plus Alex's correction): number speakers by first-SPEAKING order within that prompt, consecutively from 1, stable for every shot of the prompt. THREE builders were tagging (S<subject index>) instead - runs/build_technicolor_audio_only.py, runs/build_technicolor_ref2va.py, pipeline/refrun.py - which is only accidentally right when subjects speak in subject order (that is why S03-c01's prompt, the one Alex was reading, looked correct: Juliana is Subject 1 and speaks first). Added ONE helper core/dialogue_syntax.py (speaker_index / tag / order_from_lines) and pointed all of them plus pipeline/fullrun.py (which numbered off row['speakers']) and runs/build_t0003/4/5.py at it. BLAST RADIUS measured: 20 of the 110 dialogue chunks have a ledger  order that differs from the real first-speaking order, so lines were mislabelled in those; e.g. S06-c03 subjects {ENVOY:1, JAROL:2, TARO:3} with TARO speaking first -> correct is <Subject 3> (S1 says:), old output said (S3). Other cases: S04-c01, S08-c03, S11-c13/14/15. Verified S06-c03 now emits TARO=(S1), ENVOY=(S2), JAROL=(S3) and S03-c01 still emits (S1)/(S2) as before. NOTE for the record: on the S03 prompts Alex was looking at, the old tagging coincided with the correct answer, so that prompt's (S1)/(S2) were not themselves the mismatch - if a specific line looks mis-tagged he needs to point at it; otherwise the T0017 'Nekron speaking Juliana's lines' cause is still the missing per-shot presence clauses (arm t03 tests that). Existing arm prompts on disk (t02-t04) keep the old tagging as the record of what was rendered; new renders use the fix.

CORRECTION to my i=192 entry: the phrase 'a ledger `speakers` order' lost its backticked word to shell quoting, so it reads 'a ledger  order'. The intended sentence: 20 of the 110 dialogue chunks have a ledger `speakers` list whose order differs from the real first-speaking order, so numbering speaker ids off that list (or off the subject index) mislabels lines in those chunks. Same fact as measured; the record was just mangled in transit.
